pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks the three seeded rows are all 0 and that 2 is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test stars item 2 and expects ['First item','★ Second item','Third item']. The ★ prefix is in src/index.js `item`.
The 'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and expects only those, in id order, with a 200. The query uses WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id.
The 'AC-4' test checks both `/` and `/?show=all` return all three items in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact 'Starred only' link on `/` and the 'All items' link on the starred view.
The 'AC-6' test sends Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__. Each gets a 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred', and the 'AC-7' test asserts it. The config-check script and its shell test were updated to allow a query.

lenses.note: The spec exists and its decisions are followed: id order is kept and the view is a query parameter with no cookie.
All four state-table rows have tests that set up the state. Each test checks the list, the message and the link. The spec commit has no later edits to acceptance items.

The tests run the Worker against D1 and would fail if the behaviour were wrong. The existing traffic test fake was extended to record the query string, which loosens nothing. I did not run the tests here; CI runs them.
The README describes ?show=starred. Nothing stale found.
Input is validated against a fixed view map using Object.hasOwn. Parameterless SQL is built only from constants.
Titles are still HTML-escaped. The show value is never echoed or interpolated into SQL. The regex relaxation for routes still refuses spaces and #.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML page with no styling, assets or UI components changed. The change does not touch styling or client-side files.
The PR says no browser was available. I found no UI flow beyond two links, and the tests cover them.
The title and body match the diff: behaviour, traffic route check, migration, tests and README. Claims about CI and screenshots can't be checked from the repository.
